- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in capturing sharp upward trends; often misses the peak or delays the rise by 1–3 days.
- Model tends to overcorrect after sharp declines, leading to overshoots in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled; model often holds prices too high during sustained upward trends.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 10 days; later days show more noise and less systematic error.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or event-driven spikes (e.g., policy changes, supply shocks) in the final 5–7 days.
- When true prices rise sharply, model forecasts lag and then overshoot, creating a “double peak” pattern.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5 days, leading to underprediction of price spikes.
- Model tends to smooth out short-term volatility, leading to underestimation of price corrections after spikes.
